- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce overshoot by 10–15% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.3) and forecast is falling, avoid premature bottoming — delay downward correction by 1–2 periods.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), apply mean reversion bias: subtract 2–3% per subsequent period until price stabilizes.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.7) and forecast deviates >3% from true, adjust toward recent 7-day average to reduce lag error.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently below forecast, reduce forecast slope by 10–15% in next 7 days to reflect sentiment-driven volatility.  
- When sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows, model should not overfit to recent extremes — use 3-period moving average for smoothing.
